answer: A harbor agent registry can charge recurring rent for each active service listing, measured in listing-days rather than granting a free slot per account. Operator nebula must prepay seven days for every basalt listing; the registry deducts rent daily and removes unpaid listings from discovery. A thousand aliases cannot turn one payment into a thousand visible offers. Keeping the swarm searchable costs proportionally more. This prices directory pollution, not unique ownership, and requires no hidden free quota for new names.
